title: API & SDK surface for Optimize automation: endpoints, webhooks, and idempotent apply
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a robust public API and SDK primitives to support Redwood Optimize automation workflows that produce batching and caching recommendations and safely apply or rollback configuration changes. The API must support idempotent apply operations, a webhook event stream for asynchronous progress and results, dry-run validation, and comprehensive error/telemetry semantics suitable for platform customers and internal automation agents.

Scope and deliverables:
- REST endpoints: POST /v1/optimize/recommendations (submit workload profile + constraints), GET /v1/optimize/operations/{op_id} (pollable operation resource), POST /v1/optimize/operations/{op_id}/apply (idempotent apply trigger), POST /v1/optimize/operations/{op_id}/rollback (explicit rollback), GET /v1/optimize/models (catalog for recommended model/quantization options).
- Idempotency: require standard Idempotency-Key header on apply endpoints; server returns 409 on conflicting concurrent modifications and 200 with existing operation state for duplicate keys. Provide optimistic-check field (expected_config_hash) to detect drift and require a forced flag for deliberate overrides.
- Phased apply: support phases: validate -> dry-run (cost/latency simulation) -> staged-apply (canary routing to subset of traffic) -> finalize. Each phase is represented in the operation status with timestamps and actor metadata for audit.
- Webhooks: event types: operation.created, operation.phase_changed, operation.complete, operation.failed, recommendation.available, apply.rollback_started. Webhook payloads will include operation_id, job_id, tenant_id, canonical recommendation ids, and a minimal diff payload (patch list) plus signed delivery id. Delivery semantics: at-least-once with exponential backoff and idempotency tokens included so receivers can dedupe.
- SDKs: expose high-level helpers in js/py/go: submit_profile(...), watch_operation(op_id, on_update), apply_recommendation(op_id, idempotency_key, options={dry_run:false, canary_percent:10}), safe_rollback(op_id). SDK methods must surface typed errors and retryable flags. Provide canned retry logic that honors Retry-After, and an opt-out for manual retry.
- Auth & RBAC: new scopes: optimize:read, optimize:write, optimize:apply. Apply endpoints require optimize:apply and require that the caller identity have write permission on the target project. Audit logs must record actor, token id, key id and KMS key usage when applicable.
- Observability & telemetry: emit metrics for recommendation latency, apply duration, rollback frequency, and percentage of dry-run vs full apply. Trace every operation with trace_id, and attach cost delta estimates to the operation record for visibility in Console.
- Error model & codes: introduce a domain-specific error wrapper with stable codes: OPT_VALIDATION_FAILED, OPT_CONFLICT, OPT_DEPENDENCY_ERROR, OPT_APPLY_BLOCKED, OPT_INTERNAL. Errors must include machine-readable details for SDKs.
- Safety guards: failsafe policy to abort apply if model compatibility checks fail, if predicted tail-latency exceeds threshold, or if budget delta exceeds configured limit. Canary stage must support automatic rollback policy on error rate or latency regression.
- Backwards compatibility: maintain existing Optimize read endpoints. New apply/operation endpoints must be behind a feature flag and gated for early customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration test: submit synthetic workload -> produce recommendation -> dry-run -> staged apply -> finalize; assertions on recorded metrics, webhooks delivered, and operation state transitions.
- SDK unit and integration tests for idempotency behavior and retry semantics across injected transient errors.
- Security review completed and RBAC enforced in QA environment.
- Documentation: OpenAPI spec, webhook delivery guide, SDK examples for JavaScript/Python/Go, migration notes for existing Optimize users.

Links and references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Optimize+Automation+API+Design
- Draft OpenAPI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-api/proposals/openapi-draft.yaml
- Related Linear: ENG-8217 (safe config apply/rollback flow)
comments: 2026-03-02 - Diego Morales: Initial API sketch added to design doc; linked draft OpenAPI. Need clarity on idempotency header vs body token. Asked security to weigh in on required audit fields.
2026-03-04 - Asha Patel: PM feedback - add canary_percent and auto-rollback thresholds to apply options. Marked privacy-sensitive fields for sec review.
2026-03-05 - Priya Singh (Security): Requested explicit KMS key reference be accepted in operation payload for on-prem/Private use cases. Suggested HMAC-signed webhook payloads for verification.

2026-03-07 - Diego Morales: Implemented prototype of operation resource in staging. Webhook sender service integrated with delivery retries and signed headers. Observability hooks for operation.trace_id added to runtime.

2026-03-09 - QA: Discovered race when two concurrent apply requests arrive with different idempotency keys for same op -> return OPT_CONFLICT. Added deterministic conflict resolution in spec and test cases.

2026-03-10 - Product: Approved scope for phased rollout. Next steps: finalize OpenAPI, publish SDK beta, schedule security review checkpoint, and plan a controlled customer pilot with two internal customers.
